12. **Explicit Cauchy inference failure, (7.6) to line 336.** The proved-looking increment bound is O(1/k); the proof invokes convergence of sum 1/k^2. Bounded sequence `x_k=sin(log k)` satisfies `|x_{k+1}-x_k|<=1/k` and fails to converge. Telescoping does not repair this. A summable remainder or a separately controlled cancellation is required.

13. **Characteristic functions are outside Theorem 7.1's observable class, lines 347-350.** `exp(i<A,f>)` is not generally gauge invariant, so a theorem only about gauge-invariant observables cannot supply its limit. An underlying gauge-fixed measure construction and tightness/characteristic-functional bounds would be needed.
